blocks: Your bank refunds a stolen payment. But not this one.
One New Yorker got a call: pay your power bill today, or the lights go off. He sent one thousand, four hundred seventy-six dollars by Zelle, to an account named Con Ed Billing.
It was a scam. And according to New York's attorney general, his bank said it couldn't get that money back.
Here's why. Federal rules protect you when someone else moves your money without your permission. That's an unauthorized transfer.
But he pressed send himself. So under that definition, the payment was authorized, even though he was tricked.
The rule was written for thieves, not for tricks. Britain changed its rule in twenty twenty-four. America hasn't.
The full case, and what to do if it happens to you, is on The Rule Changed.
